findings.checklist_item: State GateCongestedError's place in the exception hierarchy (subclass of LLMError, or a new except arm added to _mcp_llm.py bodies and both CLI handlers) so the exit-11 / retryable-payload mapping actually fires.
evidence: Plan: 'GateCongestedError — an exception, never a verdict value' and 'CLI maps it to exit 11 ... MCP returns a structured {error, message, retryable: true} payload in the shape _structured_llm_failure already produces'
_mcp_llm.py:110/128 catch only `except rebar.llm.LLMError as exc: return _structured_llm_failure(exc)`
_cli/_llm_commands.py:250 catches `except llm.LLMError` (→_llm_error_exit_code, which returns 11) and `except _gate_source_error()` (SnapshotError); the plan-review CLI handler mirrors this
LLMError is `class LLMError(RuntimeError)` in src/rebar/llm/errors.py:11 — GateCongestedError is not shown to be in this hierarchy
_llm_error_exit_code returns 11 only when the raised exc carries a retryable outcome_of(); a bare non-LLMError would not even reach it
findings.finding: The plan asserts CLI maps GateCongestedError to exit 11 and MCP returns the retryable _structured_llm_failure shape, but does not state whether GateCongestedError subclasses LLMError — the fact that decides whether the existing except arms in the named edit targets catch it.
scenarios: At capacity, review_plan/verify_completion raise GateCongestedError; if it is not an LLMError subclass, the existing `except llm.LLMError` arms miss it and it propagates as a traceback / opaque tool error instead of exit 11 / retryable payload
The exit-11 path (_llm_error_exit_code) only maps to 11 when a retryable LLMOutcome is attached; a GateCongestedError with no such outcome would return 1 even if caught
findings.suggested_fix: Make GateCongestedError subclass rebar.llm.errors.LLMError and attach a retryable LLMOutcome so the existing `except llm.LLMError` arms route it to exit 11 (CLI) and _structured_llm_failure with retryable:true (MCP) without new except arms; otherwise enumerate the added except clauses in _mcp_llm.py and _cli/_llm_commands.py.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that GateCongestedError subclasses LLMError and attaches an .outcome (or explicit retryable=True) so _structured_llm_failure emits retryable:true, and pin this in the AC3 MCP-shape test.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:47 'retryable': bool(o.retryable) if o is not None else False
src/rebar/llm/failure.py:596-600 outcome_of returns getattr(error,'outcome',None) — None for an unclassified raise
src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:110,128 the structured envelope is produced only inside 'except rebar.llm.LLMError'
ABSENCE: plan does not state GateCongestedError's base class or that it carries an .outcome
findings.finding: The plan asserts the MCP payload carries 'retryable: true', but _structured_llm_failure derives 'retryable' from outcome_of(exc) (getattr(exc,'outcome',None)), defaulting to False; and it is only reached via 'except rebar.llm.LLMError'. The plan never states GateCongestedError subclasses LLMError or attaches an .outcome/LLMOutcome, so the promised retryable-true shape is not guaranteed to be produced.
findings.location: Design → Refusal ('an agent branches on retryable rather than parsing English')
scenarios: GateCongestedError is raised, does not subclass LLMError → propagates as an opaque FastMCP tool error, never reaching _structured_llm_failure
It subclasses LLMError but carries no .outcome → envelope emits retryable:false, so the agent does NOT retry the shed load

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State who creates the N slot files and when (pre-created at store init vs. deterministic fixed paths opened with O_CREAT), and confirm the naming makes each of the N slots a single stable inode so racing creators contend on the same file.
evidence: 'N slot files under the snapshot store's existing locks/ directory, each held for the run with a non-blocking fcntl.flock'
The CREATE leg of the lifecycle (who creates the N slot files, when, and with what stable naming) is not stated; only the acquire (UPDATE) and release (RETIRE) legs are.
findings.finding: The N slot files under locks/ are the shared state, but the plan does not state who CREATES the slot files or when — whether they are pre-created at store init, created lazily on first admission (open with O_CREAT), and what filename scheme distinguishes the N slots. Without a defined creation owner, two processes racing to create slot 0..N-1 could open different-inode files for the same logical slot and both acquire a flock, over-admitting past the cap.
findings.location: Design → Counter: 'N slot files under the snapshot store's existing locks/ directory'
scenarios: Two CLI gate processes start concurrently against a fresh store where locks/ has no slot files yet; if each creates and flocks its own newly-opened inode, both are admitted for the same slot and the effective cap exceeds N.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify fixed slot paths (e.g. locks/gate-slot-0 .. gate-slot-{N-1}) opened with O_CREAT, so all processes flock the same inode per slot; note that flock on the open file description handles the create-race.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the slot-selection algorithm explicitly: scan slots 0..N-1 attempting `flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)`, take the first that succeeds, and refuse (emit GateCongestedError) ONLY after all N slots fail — so contention on one slot never causes a refusal while another is free.
evidence: Plan: 'N slot files under the snapshot store's existing `locks/` directory, each held for the run with a non-blocking `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)`'

The plan states per-slot acquisition semantics but not the across-slots scan that turns N slot files into a correct cap; ABSENCE of the iterate-until-free rule leaves room for a spurious-refusal-below-capacity implementation.
AC1 verifies 'holds `limit` slots and asserts the next admission is rejected' — which passes even for a buggy scan, since the leak case is a refusal when slots ARE free, not covered by AC1/AC2.
findings.finding: The counter mechanism names 'N slot files ... each held with a non-blocking fcntl.flock', but does not specify the slot-SELECTION algorithm: how a caller scans the N files to find a free one, and that a LOCK_NB failure on one slot must fall through to try the next rather than refuse. Without an explicit 'try slots 0..N-1, first LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB success wins, only refuse after all N fail' rule, a naive single-slot or first-file-only implementation could spuriously emit GateCongestedError while free slots remain (two callers racing the same slot index), under-counting real capacity.
scenarios: Two concurrent admissions probe the same slot index first; one loses LOCK_NB and refuses even though other slots are free — a false GateCongestedError below the cap.
Implementer wires a single lockfile with a counter instead of N independent slot files, silently changing the contention semantics.
findings.suggested_fix: In the 'Counter.' paragraph add: 'Admission tries each of the N slot files in turn with LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB; the first successful acquisition is the held slot. GateCongestedError is raised only when ALL N acquisitions fail, so a LOCK_NB miss on one slot falls through to the next rather than refusing below capacity.' Consider an AC verifying that with < limit slots held, a fresh admission still succeeds regardless of which slot indices are occupied.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add one line naming the established counting-semaphore alternatives (POSIX named semaphore / posix_ipc, SysV semaphores) and why N flock slot files beat them (crash-safety via kernel fd-drop, and free REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR/dedicated-volume inheritance that a named semaphore does not get).
evidence: Plan: 'N slot files under the snapshot store's existing locks/ directory, each held ... with a non-blocking fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)'
Codebase flock uses (janitor gc/lock, _store/git_locking.py, _store/lock.py, reducer/marker.py) are all single-lock mutual exclusion, not N-slot counting — the counting composition is the novel part

Plan already grounds the fd-drop crash-safety choice in the janitor's rejected PID-heartbeat lease and external prior art (Gitaly/Sourcegraph/Bazel/ccache), so the primitive choice is well-supported; only the counting-semaphore alternative comparison is unstated
findings.finding: The N-slot-files counting semaphore is the one novel composition (rebar's existing flock uses are single-lock mutual exclusion, not N-slot counting admission); the plan justifies flock's crash-safety and tmpdir-inheritance but does not explicitly name and dismiss the established counting-semaphore alternatives (POSIX named semaphores / posix_ipc, SysV semaphores).
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer asks why N lockfiles rather than a single named semaphore with an atomic count
